aliza: Kicking off a canary for zephyr15b (int4). Using default max_new_tokens=1024. After ~2h of low traffic we're hitting OOMs on a few nodes when small bursts get coalesced into a large batch. Posting a short log snippet and config we used.

aliza: ```
2026-03-18 14:12:03 runtime ERROR OOM: alloc failed 134217728 bytes, RSS=38.4GB, kv_cache_entries=622, batch_size=18
stack: runtime::alloc -> attention_kv_alloc -> continuous_batching_commit
```

noah: saw this locally when testing with conversation replay. Frag spikes around the 6th token for long ctx. Reducing batch_size to 4 kept things alive. My read: allocator fragmentation when KV cache and prefetch touch the same pools.

sanjay: hypothesis: prefetch + int4 quant kernels cause transient large pages to be requested then freed, ending up with unusable holes. Two quick levers: lower max_new_tokens_default (to reduce KV growth) and disable prefetch for int4 models until we prove it's stable. Also consider kv-evict-threshold=0.7.

bench-bot: quick telemetry: canary nodes with prefetch=true show RSS climb to 38-39GB and p99 OOMs. prefetch=false runs peak RSS ~30-31GB. p95 latency delta +6% with prefetch off.

aliza: rolling a small runtime patch for the canary: prefetch=false, max_new_tokens_default=256, batching.window_ms=25, max_batch_tokens=8192. Will also set canary traffic to 5% on shard-3.

daria: quick mitigation on the router: add a hard token_cap per request (reject >1500 tokens with 429 + guidance) so we don't let extremely long user inputs push the system. :lock:

ops-bot: Canary config applied to shard-3: traffic=5%, runtime-config={prefetch:false,max_new_tokens_default:256,batching.window_ms:25}. Monitoring enabled.

noah: question for the runtime/quant folks — did the int4 kernel patch (the one that avoids memcpy on quant->dequant) land in the runtime used by the canary? we saw a small leak in the older patch.

sanjay: the leak was fixed in commit 0f3c9a4 but we didn't enable the optimized code path for zephyr yet (flag: enable_int4_fastkernels=false). I propose: keep fastkernels off for now, try int8 fallback if we see mem pressure, and re-enable after longer soak.

aliza: plan: 12h canary with these settings + quality eval. Conditions to progress: OOM_count==0 across canary and quality delta <=1% (on our calibrated eval set). If pass, increase to 25% and test 24h.

bench-bot: quick eval run: on the 1k-sample calibration set, int4+calibration vs fp16 baseline: ROUGE/BS avg delta = 0.6% drop, within threshold.

aliza: followups: 1) add perf-ci test to replay 10k short convo sequences with randomized max_new_tokens in [16,64,256,1024] to exercise fragmentation edge cases, 2) add a canary alert: >0 OOMs => automatic rollback, 3) document the temporary runtime flags we used.

noah: ack — i'll add the perf-ci job and the alert rule.

sanjay: I'll open a small RFC for postmortem allocator tuning (page-aligned pools, enforce kv-cache reserve on int4) and track kernel enablement after soak.

aliza: thanks all. tagging this thread for the rollout board. :white_check_mark:
